name: Hygiea
tagline: The dark carbon giant — fourth-largest asteroid and nearly a dwarf planet.

facts.label: Feature
facts.value: Nearly spherical — possibly re-formed after a giant impact

history: Hygiea is the fourth-largest body in the main belt and the darkest of the giants — a carbonaceous C-type surface reflecting barely 7% of sunlight. In 2019 VLT images showed it is almost perfectly round, a shape that suggests the original body was shattered in a catastrophic impact and re-accumulated under gravity — the same process that rounds dwarf planets. It anchors the Hygiea family, one of the belt's largest collisional groups.
